speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat
text: asked the Minister for Education (a) what is the number of international students who have defaulted on their tuition grant bond obligation in the last three years; (b) what is the amount of grants given to these defaulting students; and (c) what are the results of the recovery efforts made.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: For this small proportion of defaulters, the Ministry of Education (MOE) takes a serious view.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: It is not just a matter of money, but also of honour and trust.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: We have managed to recover from a few and we will continue to make suitable recovery efforts.

speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat (Hougang)
text: In 2016, when I asked the question, the amount of grant given to this minority group who did not fulfil their grant obligation came up to about $30 million.

speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat (Hougang)
text: Just now, the Minister said it is about $5.5 million a year now.

speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat (Hougang)
text: Can the Minister share whether there was any actual recovery in the sense that we have managed to bring it down from $30 million to $5.5 million a year now for those grants?

speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat (Hougang)
text: But then, again, these people are smart enough to gain the system and they have escaped without any consequences, so they will be smart enough not to come back here to work.

speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat (Hougang)
text: Can the Minister share on how MOE intends to recover those grants given?

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: When the Member asked the question a few years ago, we had a backlog of international students whom we were still trying to contact.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: Some were working here but they did not declare to us.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: So, at that time, we put all of them together and it came up to $30 million still being unaccounted for.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: If they want to work elsewhere, I think our enforcement cannot extend beyond those countries.
